content: {"summary":"On 11 December 2025 the SSH login to inventory-db-01 failed to write shell history because the root /var filesystem was completely full, caused by uncontrolled growth of the systemd journal logs.","likely_cause":"Unbounded journal log growth (no size limit in journald.conf) filled /var on inventory-db-01.","confidence":"high","claims":[{"text":"The shell reported a history‑file error: no space left on device.","evidence_ids":["INC-0109#0"],"quote":"shell greeted them with a history-file error: no space left on device."},{"text":"`/var` was at 100 % usage at the time of the incident.","evidence_ids":["INC-0109#0"],"quote":"`df -h /var` on the host, 100%."},{"text":"The journal directory was the dominant space consumer.","evidence_ids":["INC-0127#1"],"quote":"`/var/log/journal` at the top by a huge margin."},{"text":"The host’s `journald.conf` lacked a size limit, allowing the journal to grow unchecked.","evidence_ids":["INC-0109#1"],"quote":"journald.conf on this host had no size setting at all."}],"next_checks":["Verify that `SystemMaxUse` or similar size limits are set in `/etc/systemd/journald.conf` on all VMs with /var on the root disk.","Monitor `/var/log/journal` size daily and alert if it exceeds a safe threshold.","Check for other large log directories that might fill /var in the future."]}
